edges.relationship: Wolfe questions the reach of Fanon’s labor-dependent colonial schema in settler formations organized around Indigenous land displacement.
edges.evidence_note: Own 1999 Introduction 1–3, actual licensed publisher preview, with printed 1 and 3 visually collated. Wolfe contrasts settlers’ relative immunity to withdrawal of Indigenous labor with Fanon’s master–slave schema, citing Fanon 1967:47 and 28. He credits material grounds for optimism in particular African contexts of the 1960s and discusses Cabral alongside Fanon without equating their analyses. This is Wolfe’s qualified reading of a colonial model, not a universal rejection of Fanon or a verified description of all African or Algerian formations. The original Fanon and Cabral texts remain unread. Existing group comparison edge 1234 preserves Englert’s specific objection to Wolfe’s treatment of Fanon and Algeria; this addition does not adjudicate that disagreement.

cpl129_wolfe_1999_intro.note: Separately reviewed coverage correction: actual original 1999 Introduction 1–3 independently read again, with 1 and 3 visually collated. The qualified Fanon labor-dependent schema criticism is specific enough for the existing full Fanon endpoint; a previous missing-endpoint hold was mistaken. Cabral co-context and African contextual optimism remain explicit. Original Fanon/Cabral works unread; Englert’s separate Algeria objection retained without adjudication.

rationale: One existing-endpoint primary-source critique with contextual qualifications; old group comparison/Englert objection and all previous records preserved except one approved source-note append. Todorov hold clarified in the separate audit, no extra edge or completion.
